clue.text: Being innocent stops rowdy youth turning obstreperous

indicators.note: turning tells us to read the whole assembled string from the other end
the innocent word stops up, or plugs, the rowdy youth, so it goes inside

parts.note: a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth known for rowdiness
a naif is an innocent, unworldly person

explanation.surface: A lad who was once a harmless innocent grows into a loud, unruly teenager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' is a link. 'stops' looks like a verb about behaviour, but it puts one piece inside the other, and 'turning' then reads the whole string backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obstreperous is noisy and unruly, which is close to openly resisting or rebellious.

clue.text: Withdraw authorisation from plan?

definitions.meaning: to take away a signature, the reverse of signing off
a plan or scheme for making something

explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link. The question mark admits that the first reading is an invented word built from the prefix de- and sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A design is a scheme or drawing, a synonym of plan; split in two it suggests unsigning.

clue.text: Film-maker, dangerous and popular one

parts.note: fell is an old word meaning fierce, deadly or dangerous
in means fashionable or popular
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A movie director is described as both risky and well liked.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a dangerous, popular director; in fact the two adjectives each give a short piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico Fellini was a celebrated Italian film director, so he is an example of a film-maker.

clue.text: Perception away from Scotland Frenchman's succeeded

parts.note: awa is the Scots spelling of away
Rene is a typical French man's name, here with its possessive s
s is the standard abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone's perceptiveness, once outside Scotland, belongs to a successful Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Awareness is knowledge gained through the senses, a synonym of perception.

clue.text: Such a stilted expression of love in Shakespearean theatre

parts.note: this can stand for such, pointing to a thing of that kind
a stilted, stiff performance is called wooden
love is nil in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A clumsy, stiff declaration of love is made in an Elizabethan playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a', 'expression of' and 'in' are links. The prologue to Henry V calls the Globe playhouse 'this wooden O', after its round wooden shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from Henry V refers to the Globe, the round wooden playhouse where Shakespeare's plays were staged.

clue.text: One well-armed commander best taking our side

parts.note: OC is the military abbreviation for officer commanding
top means best, as in top marks
us is our side, the group we belong to

explanation.surface: A fully armed commander, the best there is, joins our team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is a link. 'Well-armed' suggests weapons, but it means having many arms, eight of them.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus has eight arms, so it is humorously a creature that is well armed.

clue.text: Possess topless dress

indicators.note: topless means the first letter of the dress word is cut off

parts.note: a gown is a long dress

explanation.surface: Someone is told to have a dress with no top half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes G from GOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to have it as property, a synonym of possess.

clue.text: Raising stick, pound on a drum

indicators.note: in a down clue raising means turning the piece upward, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a bat is a stick used to hit a ball
L is the abbreviation for pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: Lifting a drumstick, a musician beats on a drum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising' turns BAT to TAB; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabla is a small Indian hand drum, usually played in pairs, so it is an example of a drum.

clue.text: Chance for publicity in Stern is very attractive

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the stern word

parts.note: the poop is the raised deck at the stern of a ship
hot is slang for very attractive

explanation.surface: Someone is described as gorgeous in the German magazine Stern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link. Stern is a German magazine, which makes the capital letter misleading; here it is the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo op is a staged moment set up for press cameras, an opportunity to gain publicity.

clue.text: Very fond of books without hesitation, like Wordsworth's lass

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: without means the hesitation sound is taken out of the bookish word

parts.note: a literary person is fond of books and reading
er is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: A bookworm who no longer hesitates is compared to a girl in a Wordsworth poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking ER out of LITERARY leaves LITARY. Wordsworth's poem The Solitary Reaper describes a lone Highland girl reaping in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: The girl in The Solitary Reaper works alone, so she is solitary, which means alone.

clue.text: Pavlovian reaction I kicked in this army

indicators.note: kicked means the letter is kicked out, removed from the reaction word

parts.note: Pavlov's dogs were famous for salivation, drooling at the sound of a bell

explanation.surface: A dog's conditioned drooling, minus one letter, finds a place in an army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link. 'This army' points to the Salvation Army, the Christian charity organised like an army.
explanation.definitionFit: The Salvation Army is a Christian charity run along military lines, so the word completes the name of this army.

clue.text: Run in to prepare water for cook?

indicators.note: in tells us the run abbreviation is put inside the other piece

parts.note: to boil water is to prepare it, for tea or cooking
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone dashes inside to boil water for the cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link; 'cook' looks like a person in the surface but is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To broil is to cook with direct, intense heat, the American word for grilling.

clue.text: Announced men's appearance

indicators.note: announced means the word is said out loud and we write what is heard

parts.note: guys are men, here with the possessive dropped

explanation.surface: The arrival of the men was announced.
explanation.definitionFit: A guise is an outward form or appearance, often one that hides the truth.

clue.text: During strike, sailor is to stretch his legs

indicators.note: during means the sailor goes inside, in the middle of, the strike

parts.note: a walkout is a strike in which workers leave
AB is an able-bodied seaman, a common crossword sailor

explanation.surface: In the middle of an industrial strike, a seaman goes for a stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link. The definition is a verb phrase standing for a noun, an informal stroll; to go walkabout is a common British expression.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkabout is an informal stroll, notably one by royalty meeting crowds, a way of stretching the legs.

clue.text: Freak out as a result of not cultivating one's allotment?

definitions.text: Freak out as a result of not cultivating one's allotment?

parts.words: Freak out as a result of not cultivating one's allotment?
parts.note: an idiom for going mad, read literally as giving up your garden patch

explanation.walkthrough: An allotment is a small plot of rented land that British people grow vegetables on. The idiom read literally means losing your plot.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose the plot is British slang for to lose control or go crazy, which is to freak out.

clue.text: Zoroastrian, say, gives rocket shortly to delivery firm

indicators.note: shortly means the rocket word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a rocket is a kind of firework
a shipper is a firm that delivers goods

explanation.surface: A Zoroastrian sends a rocket off to a courier company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives' and 'to' are links. FIREWORK loses its last letter to give FIREWOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoroastrians revere fire as a symbol of purity, so a believer is called, loosely, a worshipper of flame.

clue.text: Colluding Indian gives warning

parts.note: the Inca were the native people of the Andes, South American Indians
a driver hoots, sounding the horn, to give a warning

explanation.surface: A Native American warns someone of a plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in cahoots is an idiom for working together secretly, which is colluding.

clue.text: Jack's son always goes round at a distance

definitions.note: the clue's Jack's stands for Jack is, the sailor being something

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for son in family trees

indicators.note: goes round means the always word surrounds the distance word

parts.note: e'er is the poetic short form of ever, meaning always
afar means at a distance

explanation.surface: A man's son keeps sailing around a long way off.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack, or Jack tar, is an old word for a sailor; the 's is read as is, not as a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack is old slang for a sailor, and a seafarer is someone who travels by sea.

clue.text: Dislike of union project as imprecise, so cut out

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Opposition to a plan is dismissed as vague and dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link. The union project is the European Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposition to deeper European integration, the union's project, is called Euroscepticism.

clue.text: Recreation perhaps one's taken in wild garden

indicators.note: taken in means the one letter goes inside the scrambled garden letters
wild means the garden letters run riot and are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one, with the possessive dropped

explanation.surface: A single plant is taken into an overgrown garden as a hobby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns GARDEN into READNG; 'taken in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading books is an example of a recreation, a pastime done for pleasure, hence perhaps.

clue.text: Shackleton's first volunteers had a short time in Endurance

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of the explorer's name

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
min is a minute, a short time, also its abbreviation

explanation.surface: Shackleton's first volunteers briefly served aboard his ship Endurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' and 'in' are links. Endurance was Ernest Shackleton's Antarctic ship, which makes the definition hard to spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, the ability to keep going, a synonym of endurance.

clue.text: Poor quality silver dropped in pond

indicators.note: dropped in means the silver goes into the pond word

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pond
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Inferior silver gets tossed into a pond.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or lacking, so of poor quality or amount.

clue.text: Slab of standard weight

parts.note: a standard is a flag or banner
a stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A heavy block is of the usual weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagstone is a flat paving slab of stone.

clue.text: Steps said to display elegance

indicators.note: said means the word is spoken and we write what sounds the same

parts.note: a stile is a set of steps over a fence or wall

explanation.surface: A dancer's steps are said to show grace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to display' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Style is a refined, distinctive manner, which is a synonym of elegance.

clue.text: Feel sick — having to stop vessel

definitions.meaning: the sailing term for bringing a ship to a halt

explanation.walkthrough: 'having to' means the second sense needs the word TO after it: heave to is how sailors stop a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Heave means retch when sick, and in sailing the phrase heave to means to bring a ship to a standstill.

clue.text: A little sun around at home? Not in such weather

indicators.note: around means the sun word goes round the home word

parts.note: a ray is a little sunlight, a single beam
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A glimpse of sun appears, though you would not stay at home in that weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not in' are links; the clue jokes that sun and staying in both fail on a wet day.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainy weather is wet weather, the kind with rain falling.

clue.text: Outstanding account describing a fast ship's sails?

parts.note: a bill is an account for payment
owing means outstanding, still unpaid

explanation.surface: An unpaid bill describes the sails of a fast ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse order: 'account' gives the first piece, 'Outstanding' the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Sails swelling out in a strong wind are billowing, so the word describes a fast ship's sails.

clue.text: Last item on agenda raised by native American

parts.note: AOB, any other business, is the last item on a meeting agenda

explanation.definitionFit: The boa constrictor is a snake native to the Americas.

clue.text: Scriptures I'd put separately into new grave

new means the letters of grave are made into a new order

the second of the two letters written in the clue

clue.text: Opera taking extremes of licence, but relatively accurate
